senses.gloss: (sub. בגד, חלוק) m. (orig. = לַסּוֹטָה, used as an independent w. as if from a root לסט, cmp. לָמַס) the thin web worn by loose women (= חלוק של יוצאת החוץ, Kel. XXVIII, 9, v. חוּץ II); in gen. fine veil.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:4:4">Y. Sabb. VI, 8ᵇ</cite> bot. (expl. <he>רדידים</he>, <cite ref="Isaiah 3:23">Is. III, 23</cite>) <he>ל׳ כמה דתימר וכ׳</he> it is the dress of the ill-reputed, as we read (<cite ref="Song of Songs 5:7">Cant. V, 7</cite>) they took my veil &c. (believing her to be a harlot). Ib. XIII, beg., 14ᵃ <he>וההן ל׳ אפי׳ בסוף וכ׳</he> (not <cite ref="L00588"><he>לסיטה</he></cite>) as regards the thin web, even the finishing (adding the fringe) is considered an act of weaving (in the Sabbath law).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 2:3:2">Y. M. Kat. II, 81ᵇ</cite> top <he>הורון בהדין ל׳ וכ׳</he> decided concerning (the sale of) stuff for veils (during the festive week) &c.—Pl. <he>לְסוֹטוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 4:2:6">Y. Sabb. IV, 7ᵃ</cite> top, v. <cite ref="H01417"><he>חָף</he></cite>.—Chald. form: <he>לְסוֹטַיָּיא</he>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 4:7:2">Y. B. Mets. IV, end, 9ᵈ</cite> <he>ר׳</he> … <he>הוה עסיק בל׳</he> R. A. was engaged in weaving veils.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 4:7:2">Ib.</cite> <he>מנן באילין ל׳</he> what dare we do with those veils (dare we use means to give them a fine appearance)?
